keywords.rule: Counts are papers whose title or abstract contains one of the keyword's phrases (porter-stemmed, as the theme trends); the baseline is the papers in scope first submitted in the 12 weeks before the issue, its own papers excluded. new: fewer than 5 baseline papers; rising: at least 5 papers and a rate at least 1.5 times the baseline rate; hot: at least 15 papers (and 1% of the issue) at a rate at least 0.67 times the baseline rate; steady: otherwise.
keywords.score: log2(1 + n) · log2(1 + (n + 3) / (E + 3)), E = issue papers × (baseline papers with the phrase + 0.5) / baseline papers

themes.name: LLM agents, tools, and memory
themes.summary: The papers in this theme build and evaluate the scaffolding around language-model agents: harnesses and runtimes, tool and skill interfaces, and memory systems for long-horizon, multi-session work. They differ in focus, with some proposing memory selection, scheduling, and retrieval mechanisms, others redesigning tool calling, skill retrieval, and harness compilation, and a further group benchmarking reliability, security, and failure modes of agents operating across sessions and shared environments. Several papers also examine how agents collaborate in multi-agent or human-agent teams and where such autonomy breaks down.

themes.name: World models and embodied AI
themes.summary: The papers in this theme develop and interrogate world models as predictors and rollout engines for video, driving, navigation, and manipulation, while also building embodied agents and robot policies around vision-language-action models, memory, tactile sensing, humanoids, and safety. They differ in whether they focus on generative or latent world-model architecture and diagnostics, on policy learning and control, or on benchmarks and evaluation integrity for embodied systems.

themes.name: Scientific ML and geospatial applications
themes.summary: The theme spans machine learning for geospatial and Earth-observation tasks, including urban mapping, land-cover and crop evaluation, species distribution, and geospatial foundation representations. It also includes scientific ML for physical fields and simulation, such as physics-informed neural networks, learned surrogates, inverse modeling, and generative forecasting. Papers differ by emphasizing benchmark auditing and representation transfer versus physics-constrained or generative modeling of dynamic systems.

themes.name: Reinforcement learning and optimization
themes.summary: The papers in this theme develop and analyze reinforcement learning algorithms and optimization methods, spanning policy-optimization variants, safe and constrained RL, bandits, Bayesian optimization, and bilevel or minimax formulations. A second strand provides theoretical and statistical guarantees for stochastic and Riemannian optimization, including inference, implicit bias, and convergence analysis. Applications range from pricing and retail bidding to EV charging, queueing, transit control, and biological sequence design.

themes.name: Medical imaging and clinical AI
themes.summary: This theme spans deep-learning methods across medical imaging and clinical data: image synthesis, segmentation, registration, and reconstruction, alongside vision-language models for report generation and visual question answering, plus ECG/EEG and wearable signal analysis, pathology and radiology foundation models, and interpretability and trustworthiness work. Papers differ by modality (MRI, CT, ultrasound, fundus, cytology, surgical video, waveform signals) and by strategy, ranging from generative and retrieval-augmented architectures to agents, benchmarks, and clinical decision-support frameworks.

themes.name: Efficient LLM inference and model compression
themes.summary: The papers in this theme attack the compute, memory and bandwidth cost of deploying large and multimodal models, spanning depth and structured pruning, post-training and low-bit quantization, KV-cache selection and recomputation, speculative decoding, distillation, and serving or caching systems. They differ in whether they target the weights themselves, the attention and KV working set, the drafter/verification loop, or the scheduling and hardware mapping of inference, with several papers focused specifically on edge devices, mobile GPUs, TPUs, and vision-language workloads.

themes.name: Vision-language and multimodal learning
themes.summary: The papers cover multimodal embedding surveys, vision-language benchmarks and diagnostics, video and streaming question answering, grounding, OCR/document parsing, multimodal fusion, and reinforcement-learning post-training for MLLMs. They differ in whether they contribute representation methods, evaluation protocols, data-centric pipelines, or deployment-oriented tuning. Several works specifically probe gaps between what multimodal models can perceive and what they can reliably use.

themes.name: Diffusion, flow, and video generation
themes.summary: The papers span diffusion and flow generative modeling for images and video, focusing on efficiency, controllability, physical consistency, long-video memory, and faithful evaluation. They range from training-free acceleration and one-step or flow-map methods to autoregressive long-video context management, camera and motion control, inverse-problem priors, theory, and deployment. They differ in whether they target image or video, learned versus training-free approaches, and quality or fidelity versus speed and physical plausibility.

themes.name: Reasoning and LLM verification
themes.summary: The papers examine how LLM reasoning can be verified, monitored, and made reliable, spanning formal proof and theorem generation, proof repair, chain-of-thought oversight, and judge- or verifier-based evaluation. They differ in whether they build benchmarks and audits of verification failures, propose training or prompting methods to improve reasoning, or analyze the certifiability and robustness of model outputs. Several focus on distinguishing genuine reasoning gains from selection artifacts, reward hacking, confabulation, and gaming of verifiers.

themes.name: Fairness, bias, and auditing
themes.summary: This theme collects work that diagnoses, measures, and mitigates bias and unfairness across a wide range of models and settings, from frozen vision-language models and facial expression recognition to plant disease detectors, private image generators, language models, and decision and auction systems. The papers differ in approach: some audit disparities empirically, some build protocols and benchmarks for auditing, some propose mitigation methods such as concept erasure, activation steering, or privacy- and fairness-aware training, and others develop fairness-aware learning theory for classification, bandits, ranking, and experimental design.

themes.name: Retrieval-augmented generation and knowledge grounding
themes.summary: The papers in this theme build, evaluate, and critique retrieval-augmented generation and knowledge grounding across many settings, including scientific figure QA, embodied memory, book-length cross-chapter questions, medical speech QA, web search, and compliance auditing. They differ in whether they contribute new retrieval architectures or embeddings, benchmarks and diagnostic evaluations, or methods that convert retrieved knowledge into parametric memory or tighter evidence control. A recurring concern is whether retrieved or cited evidence actually supports the answer, spanning evidence attribution, evidence bypass, and cross-topic name collisions.

themes.name: Object detection, tracking, and segmentation
themes.summary: This theme's papers build detection, tracking, and segmentation systems for constrained and adverse real-world settings, ranging from lightweight mobile YOLO models and pedestrian obstacle warnings to aerial small-object detection, X-ray security screening, autonomous-driving weather robustness, and adversarial maritime surveillance. They also cover UAV and out-of-view tracking, video action detection, amodal and ecological segmentation, connectomics error correction, and pose or facial landmark estimation. The differences lie in modality, deployment hardware, and the specific failure mode addressed, such as occlusion, label noise, tiny objects, domain shift, or out-of-view motion.

highlights.title: From Fragmentation to Fusion: A Survey and Roadmap for Omnimodal Embeddings
highlights.authors: Ziyin Zhang, Yuyu Guo, Ying Zhang et al.
highlights.why: Provides a unified cross-cutting roadmap for omnimodal embeddings, an important survey for the field.
highlights.key_result: The paper proposes a framework of three progressively harder capabilities—coverage, comparability, and compositionality—and three paths toward unification that satisfy these in turn: transformation broadens coverage, alignment enables comparability, and joint embedding, the terminus the authors advocate, aims at compositionality; it presents itself as the first unified, cross-cutting treatment of omnimodal embedding research. It also quantifies the fragmentation it diagnoses: a combined analysis of 1,352 formally published embedding papers and a decade of arXiv preprints shows works that explicitly cross modality boundaries account for under 5% of both samples.
evidence: To reason across this convergence without conflating it, we propose a framework of three progressively harder capabilities: coverage, comparability, and compositionality. Three paths toward unification satisfy these in turn: transformation broadens coverage, alignment enables comparability, and joint embedding, the terminus we advocate, aims at compositionality. This position paper traces the resulting evolution, providing the first unified, cross-cutting treatment of omnimodal embedding research.

A combined analysis of 1,352 formally published embedding papers (2023--2025) and a decade of arXiv preprints (2015--2025) indicates that the overwhelming majority of embedding research is single-modality, each modality publishing in its home community's venues, while works that explicitly cross modality boundaries account for under 5% of both samples and emerge only recently.

highlights.title: OCELOT: Planetary-Scale Species Distribution Modeling with Satellite Foundation Embeddings
highlights.authors: Bart van Merrienboer, Lauren Harrell, Keith Anderson et al.
highlights.why: Scales species distribution modeling to 2B records and 100k taxa, enabling remote-region extrapolation with satellite foundation embeddings.
highlights.key_result: OCELOT fuses spatial coordinates with satellite foundation embeddings and is trained on 2 billion GBIF records across 100,000 taxa; satellite foundation embeddings improve extrapolation by 51% over coordinate-only models and outperform classical bioclimatic rasters. The resulting model also matches or outperforms existing baselines on established interpolation benchmarks.
evidence: We scale relative occurrence species distribution models by training a multimodal implicit neural representation network called OCELOT that fuses spatial coordinates with satellite foundation embeddings on two orders of magnitude more observations than previous work: 2 billion GBIF records across 100,000 taxa.

To evaluate performance in remote areas, we benchmark geographic extrapolation using the NDCG metric on spatial block holdouts up to 600 km. Satellite foundation embeddings improve extrapolation by 51% over coordinate-only models and outperform classical bioclimatic rasters.

The resulting model also matches or outperforms existing baselines on established interpolation benchmarks, demonstrating that optimizing for geographic extrapolation does not compromise in-distribution accuracy.

highlights.why: Using generative outpainting as world-model prior for out-of-view tracking is a surprising reframing with 3x improvement.

highlights.title: Integer-Exact Microscaling: Running MXFP4 Language Models on INT8 Matrix Units
highlights.authors: Shinyoung Kang, Junhyung Ahn, Yujun Kim et al.
highlights.theme: Efficient LLM inference and model compression
highlights.why: Enables MXFP4 models on INT8 matrix units with exact integer GEMM, practical gains on Apple hardware.
highlights.key_result: We show when no per-block work is needed: a row of MXFP4 weights is exactly one INT8 vector times one power-of-two scale if its block exponents span at most three, so a linear layer becomes a single INT8 GEMM with one rescale per output. Enforcing the condition adds at most 1/16 of a row's largest rounding error to the blocks it changes, and real weights already satisfy it: 97.9--99.97% of rows across seven models, including 99.93% of the 95M rows of a 125B-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) model, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.

news.title: Rewarding defenders with bigger bug bounties
news.summary: OpenAI said it is raising Security Bug Bounty rewards, more than quadrupling the midpoint of reward ranges for medium, high, and critical findings on average; a critical vulnerability in core products such as ChatGPT, Codex, or the API Platform will earn up to $30,000, with exceptional critical findings eligible for up to $100,000 and up to $172,000 with bonuses. It also introduced quality bonus multipliers, a 5-tier loyalty bonus program, priority campaign multipliers, and retroactive payments for some prior reports, and said its security team will be at PROMPT2PWN in Oakland on November 20–21.

news.title: Preparing our next security sprint to harden OpenAI
news.summary: OpenAI said it is planning its next internal security sprint with security partner Cathedral, whose researchers will use OpenAI models alongside OpenAI teams to test defenses. It said its last sprint dedicated 25% of product engineers to finding and fixing weaknesses, that it is more than quadrupling rewards for critical bug bounty findings, and that it has committed $1 billion in subsidized access over six months for frontline defenders via Daybreak customers.

news.title: Scaling Git at OpenAI
news.summary: OpenAI introduced Pando, a new Git backend that now powers all development in its monorepo while retaining Git protocol and client compatibility, designed for horizontally scalable writes and high read throughput. In production, Pando cut median push latency by nearly 5x and delivers nearly a petabyte of Git data per day.

news.title: Introducing the Grid Protectors Program
news.summary: OpenAI launched the Grid Protectors Program, a national effort to work with utilities, regulators, and policymakers so future compute campuses can reduce electricity demand when the grid is under strain. It cited U.S. data center capacity projected to exceed 100 gigawatts by 2030 and said its Georgia Power agreement includes up to 1,000 megawatts of flexible demand response, equivalent to roughly 700,000 households, with the Effingham County campus committed to pay full infrastructure and electric-service costs.

news.title: The latest AI news we announced in October 2026
news.summary: Google recapped October AI updates including the global rollout of Gemini 4 Argon, a frontier reasoning model, and the announcement two weeks later of Gemini 4 Carbon, which is in pre-release testing with the U.S. government and trusted cyber defenders via the Fairwind Program. It also introduced Genie 4 for real-time interactive world simulation with native audio and expanded SynthID Detector globally in English after watermarking more than 180 billion images and videos and 240,000 years of audio.

news.title: Diagnose Distributed AI Workload Failures with NVIDIA Attribution
news.summary: NVIDIA released NVIDIA Attribution, an open-source tool that correlates workload-scoped logs, metrics, telemetry, and scheduler state into a structured diagnosis with outcome, root cause, affected nodes, symptoms, and evidence trail. It comprises an Attribution Service with a REST API and an Attribution Blueprint Python orchestrator with connectors for Slurm, Kueue, Loki, local files, Kubernetes pod logs, and PromQL, and NVIDIA says it is used in production to analyze millions of workloads weekly across hundreds of thousands of GPUs.

news.title: Keep Distributed Training Running with Automated Workload Recovery
news.summary: NVIDIA introduced NVIDIA Recovery, an open-source workload-level service that automates recovery across cluster training jobs by detecting interruptions from application logs, GPU metrics, and scheduler signals and coordinating isolation and checkpoint restarts. It integrates with Slurm via a Helm-deployable Advisor Controller, starts new deployments in monitor mode, keeps a persistent audit trail, and in production monitoring from July 9 to October 9 covered nearly 200 jobs per day with approximately 8,550 anomaly detections and mean detection and recovery-action latencies of 69 and 94 seconds.

news.title: Making Kubernetes AI-Ready for NVIDIA Vera Rubin on Day One
news.summary: NVIDIA described AICR recipes for making Kubernetes ready for Vera Rubin NVL72, including validated choices for the R615.23 open-kernel-module driver, DRA driver v0.5.0 with ComputeDomains, Ubuntu 26.04 with a 64k-page kernel, and GPU Operator v26.7.0. Validation passed deployment, conformance, and a cross-node NCCL all-reduce gate at 744.71 GB/s bus bandwidth at 16 GiB over NVLink, and early silicon testing surfaced an unmapped Rubin architecture value in go-nvlib that crash-looped the DRA kubelet plugin and was fixed in DRA driver v0.5.0.

news.title: Build World Models for Interactive Simulation with NVIDIA Cosmos
news.summary: NVIDIA described Cosmos as a platform of world foundation models and development tools for physical AI, with Cosmos Framework offering modular open tools for training, reinforcement learning, optimization, and inference across models including Cosmos 3, NVIDIA Alpamayo, GR00T, Qwen, and pi0.5. Cosmos 3 Nano recipes generate synchronized camera video and LiDAR observations, Cosmos NIM microservices deliver roughly 2–3x speedups on H200 GPUs, and Cosmos3-Nano generation needs 58 GiB in BF16 and 44 GiB in FP8 with offloading.

news.title: Prepare web content for Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases with Crawl4AI
news.summary: AWS described how to prepare web content for Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases using the managed Web Crawler connector or a custom Crawl4AI preparation path that writes Markdown and metadata sidecars to Amazon S3 for ingestion. The Crawl4AI path supports structured Markdown pruning, bounded extraction with CSS selectors and crawl limits, custom metadata, and works with managed or customer-managed knowledge bases for batch ingestion of known web properties.

news.title: Build efficient agents with knowledge distillation on Amazon SageMaker AI
news.summary: AWS described using sequence-level knowledge distillation (SeqKD) on Amazon SageMaker AI to fine-tune a smaller shopping agent on multi-step trajectories generated by a frontier teacher model, keeping trajectories that solve the task for supervised fine-tuning. The approach needs only teacher text, no teacher logits or reinforcement-learning infrastructure, and the post covers trajectory generation, training on serverless infrastructure, and evaluation against a held-out benchmark.

news.title: Agentic engineering intelligence with Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
news.summary: AWS described a multi-agent engineering assistant for aerospace part substitution built with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings, and the open source Strands Agents SDK, using a planner to route queries to Catalog, Evaluation, and Knowledge specialists. The system uses deterministic Python tolerance rules for spec-fit scoring, keeps the engineer as decision-maker, drafts justification memos and Integration Impact Assessments, and writes audit trail entries aligned with AS9100 sections 8.4 and 8.5.6.

news.title: How Circle K accelerated DevOps incident triage to under 15 minutes with Amazon Bedrock
news.summary: Circle K built an automated DevOps incident triage system on Amazon Bedrock using an agentic AI architecture that investigates incidents and delivers structured summaries to Slack, reducing mean triage time to under 15 minutes, a 67–75 percent reduction based on internal incident-response metrics. Circle K operates more than 17,200 convenience and fuel retail stores across 27 countries and migrated the system from Amazon Bedrock Flows to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.

themes.name: 世界模型与具身 AI

themes.name: 高效 LLM 推理与模型压缩

highlights.title: Wave Forcing: Towards Speed-of-Light Streaming Video Generation
highlights.authors: Yijie Jin, Yuxuan Liu, Jiajun Xu et al.
highlights.why: 共同设计训练和运行时，用于每轮处理一个 chunk 的流式视频生成，以有原则的方式解决速度和长视频质量问题。
highlights.key_result: 在 Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B 上的实验表明，5-step WF 在保持与 Rolling Forcing 相当的整体质量的同时，在短和长视频上获得了更高的 Dynamic Degree。我们的系统效率实验表明，在八块 H200 GPU 上，4-step WF 达到 147.6 DiT FPS 和 134.8 端到端 FPS，产生单 GPU 端到端吞吐量的 7.07 倍。
evidence: Experiments on Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B show that 5-step WF maintains overall quality comparable to Rolling Forcing while achieving higher Dynamic Degree on both short and long videos. Our system efficiency experiments show that 4-step WF achieves 147.6 DiT FPS and 134.8 end-to-end FPS on eight H200 GPUs, yielding 7.07 the single-GPU end-to-end throughput.

highlights.title: Satisfied, Not Solving: Wireheading of Bounded Homeostatic Rewards in Reinforcement Learning
highlights.why: 预先注册的实验推翻了有界稳态奖励能抵抗利用的假设，表明智能体会发生 wirehead 并无法完成任务。
highlights.key_result: 有界信号的 wireheading 跨任务复现（Section ）。通过一个廉价的篡改动作，PPO 在 r4.solve.on 种子下解决了 DoorKey-8x8，而同样的种子在 r4.solve.off 且没有该动作时未解决；在 KeyCorridorS3R1 上 r5.solve.C5 对比 r5.solve.C1 也如此。
evidence: Wireheading of a bounded signal replicates across tasks (Section ). With a cheap tamper action, PPO solved DoorKey-8x8 in r4.solve.on seeds against r4.solve.off on the same seeds without it, and KeyCorridorS3R1 in r5.solve.C5 against r5.solve.C1.

highlights.title: From Fragmentation to Fusion: A Survey and Roadmap for Omnimodal Embeddings
highlights.authors: Ziyin Zhang, Yuyu Guo, Ying Zhang et al.
highlights.why: 为全模态嵌入提供了统一的跨领域路线图，是该领域一篇重要综述。
highlights.key_result: 本文提出了一个由三种逐步更难的能力——覆盖性、可比性和组合性——构成的框架，以及三条依次满足这些能力的统一路径：变换扩大覆盖性，对齐实现可比性，作者倡导的终点 joint embedding 则瞄准组合性；本文自称是首个对全模态嵌入研究的统一、跨领域处理。它还量化了其诊断出的碎片化：对 1,352 篇正式发表的嵌入论文和十年 arXiv 预印本的联合分析显示，明确跨越模态边界的工作在两个样本中均占不到 5%。
evidence: To reason across this convergence without conflating it, we propose a framework of three progressively harder capabilities: coverage, comparability, and compositionality. Three paths toward unification satisfy these in turn: transformation broadens coverage, alignment enables comparability, and joint embedding, the terminus we advocate, aims at compositionality. This position paper traces the resulting evolution, providing the first unified, cross-cutting treatment of omnimodal embedding research.

A combined analysis of 1,352 formally published embedding papers (2023--2025) and a decade of arXiv preprints (2015--2025) indicates that the overwhelming majority of embedding research is single-modality, each modality publishing in its home community's venues, while works that explicitly cross modality boundaries account for under 5% of both samples and emerge only recently.

highlights.title: Democratizing Robot-Use Agents: A Unified Harness with Open Models
highlights.authors: Jiarui Yuan, Yuxin Zuo, Xiaoyu Huang et al.
highlights.why: 开放权重 harness 超越了专有基线，使机器人使用智能体的研究可训练且更易获取。
highlights.key_result: 在没有特权输入的情况下，开箱即用的 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 取得了 31.39 的 RoboDojo Score，超过了已公布的 GPT-6 Astra–RoboProbe 的 28.97 结果以及许多 VLA/WAM 基线，并在 19 个现实世界任务上表现具有竞争力。
evidence: Without privileged inputs, an out-of-the-box Qwen3.8-Flash-Next achieves a RoboDojo Score of 31.39, surpassing the published GPT-6 Astra–RoboProbe result of 28.97 and many VLA/WAM baselines, and performs competitively on 19 real-world tasks.

highlights.title: OCELOT: Planetary-Scale Species Distribution Modeling with Satellite Foundation Embeddings
highlights.authors: Bart van Merrienboer, Lauren Harrell, Keith Anderson et al.
highlights.why: 将物种分布建模扩展到 2B 条记录和 100k 个分类群，利用卫星基础嵌入实现偏远区域外推。
highlights.key_result: OCELOT 将空间坐标与卫星基础嵌入融合，并在 100,000 个分类群的 2 billion 条 GBIF 记录上训练；卫星基础嵌入比仅用坐标的模型将外推性能提高 51%，并优于经典生物气候栅格。所得模型在既有插值基准上也达到或超过现有基线。
evidence: We scale relative occurrence species distribution models by training a multimodal implicit neural representation network called OCELOT that fuses spatial coordinates with satellite foundation embeddings on two orders of magnitude more observations than previous work: 2 billion GBIF records across 100,000 taxa.

To evaluate performance in remote areas, we benchmark geographic extrapolation using the NDCG metric on spatial block holdouts up to 600 km. Satellite foundation embeddings improve extrapolation by 51% over coordinate-only models and outperform classical bioclimatic rasters.

The resulting model also matches or outperforms existing baselines on established interpolation benchmarks, demonstrating that optimizing for geographic extrapolation does not compromise in-distribution accuracy.

highlights.title: On the Limits of Test-Time Compute for Self-Evaluation
highlights.authors: Anirudh Buvanesh, Khaled Rouissi, Sujin Yun et al.
highlights.why: 对自评估排序误差进行了偏差-方差分析，并引入 Scorpio，改进验证和聚合。
highlights.key_result: 在数学、代码和谜题基准上，Scorpio 改进了验证、树搜索和聚合。在验证方面，Scorpio 比最强基线将准确率最多提高 7 个百分点，同时在推理成本降低 17–42% 的情况下达到或超过该基线的峰值准确率。
evidence: Across math, code, and puzzle benchmarks, Scorpio improves verification, tree search, and aggregation. For verification, Scorpio improves accuracy over the strongest baseline by up to 7 percentage points while matching or exceeding that baseline’s peak accuracy with 17--42% lower inference cost.

highlights.title: TAP-Out: Tracking Any Point in 360{\deg} via Outpainting
highlights.authors: Finlay G. C. Hudson, James A. D. Gardner, William A. P. Smith
highlights.why: 利用生成式外绘作为世界模型先验进行视野外跟踪是一种令人惊讶的重构，带来了 3x 的改进。
highlights.key_result: 在 TAPVid360 基准上，TAP-Out 取得了最先进的性能，将 OOV 跟踪准确率比之前最好的方法提高了约 3；在 ground-truth (GT) 相机下，其最显著的优势体现在 OOV 点上：^x_ avg,oof = 0.332，大约比 CoTracker360 的 0.106 高 3.1。
evidence: On the TAPVid360 benchmark, TAP-Out achieves state-of-the-art performance, improving OOV tracking accuracy by approximately 3 over the best prior method.

TAP-Out with ground-truth (GT) cameras achieves state-of-the-art performance across all metrics. The most pronounced advantage is on OOV points: ^x_ avg,oof = 0.332, approximately 3.1 higher than CoTracker360's 0.106. This validates that explicit scene completion produces more accurate OOV tracks than implicit direction prediction.

highlights.title: Integer-Exact Microscaling: Running MXFP4 Language Models on INT8 Matrix Units
highlights.authors: Shinyoung Kang, Junhyung Ahn, Yujun Kim et al.
highlights.theme: Efficient LLM inference and model compression
highlights.why: 在 INT8 矩阵单元上以精确整数 GEMM 运行 MXFP4 模型，在 Apple 硬件上实现实际收益。
highlights.key_result: We show when no per-block work is needed: a row of MXFP4 weights is exactly one INT8 vector times one power-of-two scale if its block exponents span at most three, so a linear layer becomes a single INT8 GEMM with one rescale per output. Enforcing the condition adds at most 1/16 of a row's largest rounding error to the blocks it changes, and real weights already satisfy it: 97.9--99.97% of rows across seven models, including 99.93% of the 95M rows of a 125B-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) model, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.
evidence: We show when no per-block work is needed: a row of MXFP4 weights is exactly one INT8 vector times one power-of-two scale if its block exponents span at most three, so a linear layer becomes a single INT8 GEMM with one rescale per output. Enforcing the condition adds at most 1/16 of a row's largest rounding error to the blocks it changes, and real weights already satisfy it: 97.9--99.97% of rows across seven models, including 99.93% of the 95M rows of a 125B-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) model, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.

news.title: Rewarding defenders with bigger bug bounties
news.summary: OpenAI said it is raising Security Bug Bounty rewards, more than quadrupling the midpoint of reward ranges for medium, high, and critical findings on average; a critical vulnerability in core products such as ChatGPT, Codex, or the API Platform will earn up to $30,000, with exceptional critical findings eligible for up to $100,000 and up to $172,000 with bonuses. It also introduced quality bonus multipliers, a 5-tier loyalty bonus program, priority campaign multipliers, and retroactive payments for some prior reports, and said its security team will be at PROMPT2PWN in Oakland on November 20–21.

news.title: Preparing our next security sprint to harden OpenAI
news.summary: OpenAI 表示计划与安全合作伙伴 Cathedral 开展下一次内部安全冲刺，其研究人员将与 OpenAI 团队一起使用 OpenAI 模型测试防御。该公司称上一次冲刺投入了 25% 的产品工程师来发现和修复弱点，正在将关键漏洞发现奖励提高四倍以上，并已承诺在六个月内通过 Daybreak 客户为一线防御者提供 $1 billion 的补贴访问。

news.title: Scaling Git at OpenAI
news.summary: OpenAI 推出了 Pando，这是一种新的 Git 后端，现在支持其单一代码仓库中的所有开发，同时保留 Git 协议和客户端兼容性，专为水平扩展写入和高读取吞吐量设计。在生产环境中，Pando 将中位推送延迟降低了近 5x，并且每天传输近一个拍字节的 Git 数据。

news.title: Introducing the Grid Protectors Program
news.summary: OpenAI 启动了 Grid Protectors Program，这是一项与公用事业公司、监管机构和政策制定者合作的国家级努力，旨在使未来的计算园区在电网紧张时减少用电需求。公司引用了到 2030 年美国数据中心容量预计将超过 100 gigawatts 的数据，并表示其 Georgia Power 协议包括最多 1,000 megawatts 的灵活需求响应，相当于约 700,000 个家庭，Effingham County 园区承诺支付全部基础设施和电力服务费用。

news.title: The latest AI news we announced in October 2026
news.summary: Google recapped October AI updates including the global rollout of Gemini 4 Argon, a frontier reasoning model, and the announcement two weeks later of Gemini 4 Carbon, which is in pre-release testing with the U.S. government and trusted cyber defenders via the Fairwind Program. It also introduced Genie 4 for real-time interactive world simulation with native audio and expanded SynthID Detector globally in English after watermarking more than 180 billion images and videos and 240,000 years of audio.

news.title: Diagnose Distributed AI Workload Failures with NVIDIA Attribution
news.summary: NVIDIA 发布了 NVIDIA Attribution，这是一个开源工具，将工作负载范围内的日志、指标、遥测和调度器状态关联成结构化诊断，包括结果、根因、受影响节点、症状和证据链。它包含带 REST API 的 Attribution Service 和一个 Attribution Blueprint Python 编排器，该编排器带有用于 Slurm、Kueue、Loki、本地文件、Kubernetes pod 日志和 PromQL 的连接器，NVIDIA 表示其已在生产环境中每周分析数百万个工作负载，覆盖数十万个 GPU。

news.title: Keep Distributed Training Running with Automated Workload Recovery
news.summary: NVIDIA introduced NVIDIA Recovery, an open-source workload-level service that automates recovery across cluster training jobs by detecting interruptions from application logs, GPU metrics, and scheduler signals and coordinating isolation and checkpoint restarts. It integrates with Slurm via a Helm-deployable Advisor Controller, starts new deployments in monitor mode, keeps a persistent audit trail, and in production monitoring from July 9 to October 9 covered nearly 200 jobs per day with approximately 8,550 anomaly detections and mean detection and recovery-action latencies of 69 and 94 seconds.

news.title: Making Kubernetes AI-Ready for NVIDIA Vera Rubin on Day One
